headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy to propose tariffs that allocate certain capacity and distribution infrastructure costs to large energy users, aiming to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, HB 1393, aims to shift certain electric grid upgrade costs, including capacity market costs and distribution infrastructure, to data centers and other large energy users. This shift is projected to save typical residential customers over $5.50 a month, while increasing bills for data center customers by about 15%.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, enhancing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers Across Virginia
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, including reclaimed water. This legislation aims to provide better data on the industry's water use, which can be millions of gallons daily, to inform state and local planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to require assessments of other environmental impacts for new high energy use data centers.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (potential for increased regulatory hurdles).
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Noise and Siting Studies
news_summary: A new Virginia law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct site assessments examining noise profiles on nearby homes and schools. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, but it empowers localities to require additional impact assessments.
